At 6½ miles, the two Georges, Oliver and Beecham, after their excellent County performances, were in 29th and 31st positions, with Hugh McGreechan 33rd, Garry Warr 38th, George Checkley 43rd, Percy Wright 44th, Harry Kemp 58th, Bob…
Evans of Highgate, walking as an individual, R. Goodall and Brian Hawkins. Syd James was ruled out roughly half way which seriously affected our chances of winning the Berman Cup.

Three teams were entered from the club and again they continued to show progress, the highlight being the 3rd place of Syd James who walked exceptionally well and showed that he can satisfy the judges. Brian Hawkins of the Met.
After the 10 laps we moved out on to the road with George leading from Bryan Hawkins and myself, Bob Goodall, McFarlane, and Don Thompson with the French team.

Our walkers journeyed to Eltham for this race on 10th December and once again showed considerable improvement over their previous efforts. Eric Hall walked an exceptionally fine race to finish second to B.

George was second in 14.15 and the rest of the field, including Brian Hawkins of the Met. were never in the same street. So ended another Southern Championships Gratifying in some ways, but definitely disappointing in others.
For the first time Metropolitan W.C. sent a strong team for this race and Hawkins, Hutchison and Nigel Thompson battled for the first three placings the whole way, eventually finishing in that order.
